clue.text: Repeatedly use machete with expedition

indicators.note: repeatedly tells us the action is done twice, so the word is written two times over

parts.note: to use a machete is to chop

explanation.surface: Someone hacks their way through the jungle with a machete on an expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expedition' looks like a journey, but here it means speed, as in 'with all expedition'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubled chop is an informal cry meaning quickly, and expedition means promptness or speed.

clue.text: He will make a hole in which to put European plant

indicators.note: the European is to be put into the middle of the other pieces, so these words signal a container

parts.note: contracted to he'll, written without the apostrophe
to bore is to make a hole by drilling

explanation.surface: A gardener says he will dig a hole to plant something from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He will' is contracted with the apostrophe dropped; 'make a hole' is a verb phrase, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellebore is a flowering plant, the Christmas rose and its relatives, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Line on artist whose opening was a disaster?

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on top of another comes first, so these words set the order

parts.note: P and O, written P&O, is a well-known British shipping line
RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A drawing line is added by a painter whose exhibition opening flopped.
explanation.walkthrough: P&O is a British shipping and ferry company, spelt out as P AND O; 'on' puts it above RA in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the woman given a jar opened it and released all evils into the world, so her opening was a disaster.

clue.text: Tried diligently, putting in extra energy

indicators.note: an extra letter is put inside another word, so these words signal a container

parts.note: to work hard is to work diligently
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone made a diligent effort, putting in extra energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tried' looks like 'attempted', echoing the surface, but it is the courtroom sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A case that has been tried in court has been heard by the judge, the legal sense of the verb.

clue.text: Brief piece of writing standard for course

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: para is the short form of paragraph, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A short written piece sets the standard for a course of study.
explanation.walkthrough: The course is a golf course, not a course of study.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the standard number of strokes for a golf hole or the whole course.

clue.text: American scholars having removed chapter that's erroneous

indicators.note: the scholars have taken out one letter, so these words signal a deletion

parts.note: in American usage the faculty is the teaching staff of a college

explanation.surface: US academics cut a chapter that contained a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Something faulty is defective or wrong, a synonym for erroneous.

clue.text: Counterfeit draft user, perhaps

indicators.note: counterfeit means faked or forged, so the following letters are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone who passes forged drafts, a kind of cheque, is a cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: A draft is a banker's order to pay; someone using a forged one is the answer, so the whole clue serves as definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheat who uses fake banker's drafts is a swindler, a person committing fraud.

clue.text: Bold newcomer riding over jump

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second, so these words set the order

parts.note: a jockey who is up is riding the horse
to start is to jump in surprise

explanation.surface: A brash new jockey rides his horse over a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jump' looks like a fence for the horse, but it means a sudden start.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is a person who has risen suddenly and behaves arrogantly, a cheeky newcomer.

clue.text: Stratagem, capturing rook with check

indicators.note: capturing means taking a piece inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: to tick a list is to check it
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess ploy captures a rook and gives check.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture misleads: check is a tick mark, not a threat to the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A trick is a cunning ploy or ruse, a synonym for stratagem.

clue.text: Architect's drawing of flat unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is left off

parts.note: a plane is a flat surface

explanation.surface: An architect's drawing of an apartment is left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment, matching the architect, but it is an adjective meaning level.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a scale drawing of a building seen from above, as an architect produces.

clue.text: Need for pilot in vessel East of new marina

indicators.note: in an across answer east is to the right, so the vessel follows
new means remade, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

parts.note: a ship is a sea vessel

explanation.surface: A pilot is needed for a boat at a newly built harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pilot' suggests a harbour pilot guiding the vessel into the marina, but here it is an aircraft pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmanship is skill in flying an aircraft, something every pilot requires.

clue.text: Used support and help

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
to give a hand is to help

explanation.surface: Someone offers backing and assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used' looks like a verb, but it is an adjective meaning not new.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand goods have had a previous owner, so they are used.

clue.text: Making waves in a way listeners can appreciate

definitions.text: Making waves in a way listeners can appreciate

parts.words: Making waves in a way listeners can appreciate
parts.note: making waves suggests causing trouble, but here the waves are sound waves, which an audience can hear

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up trouble in a way the public approve of.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done so it can be heard creates sound waves that listeners pick up.

clue.text: Fliers, one going the other way

indicators.note: going the other way means travelling in reverse, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: one of the fliers, the skua, a predatory seabird

explanation.surface: A flock of birds is in flight, but one heads in the opposite direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' means one kind of flier; the skua, turned round, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Auks are diving seabirds such as puffins and guillemots, and most of them fly.

clue.text: Chap into regressive house style that's dated

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the chap is placed within the other word
regressive means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: decor is the style of a house's furnishing
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: A man moves into a house with old-fashioned decor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regressive' turns DECOR into ROCED; MAN goes 'into' it. 'dated' looks like old-fashioned but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To have romanced someone is to have courted or gone out with them, which is what dated means.

clue.text: Appeared pale guarding king, fearful of being shot

indicators.note: guarding means surrounding something to protect it, so the king sits within the other pieces

parts.note: to have come is to have appeared
ashy means pale, the colour of ash
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king's bodyguard looked pale, afraid of being shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests gunfire, but it means photographed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone camera-shy dislikes being photographed, and a shot is a photograph.

clue.text: Computer enthusiast, over time, liable to blow a fuse

indicators.note: over means covering, so the enthusiast spreads across the time letter

parts.note: a techy is someone keen on computers and gadgets

explanation.surface: A computer geek who works too long might blow a fuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow a fuse' fits the computer picture but means lose one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetchy person is irritable and quick to anger, apt to lose their temper.

clue.text: Best part of Oxford street fair

parts.note: the High Street in Oxford is known simply as the High
fair hair or skin is light

explanation.surface: The best attraction on an Oxford street is a fair.
explanation.walkthrough: The High is the main street of Oxford, the English university city.
explanation.definitionFit: A highlight is the most memorable or outstanding part of something.

clue.text: Cable broadcast might, initially, take the wind out of one's sails

definitions.text: take the wind out of one's sails

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order
initially means at the start, so the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A cable TV programme might deflate someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns CABLE into BECAL; 'initially' gives M from 'might'.
explanation.definitionFit: To becalm a ship is to leave it without wind, literally taking the wind from its sails.

clue.text: One more article not by that woman

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
taken as written
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: An extra item is not written by her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a piece of writing, but it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means an additional one, one more of the same.

clue.text: Composers, one heard, providing arrangement of bars for singer

indicators.note: one of the composers is to be heard said aloud, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: William Byrd was an English Renaissance composer
John Cage was an American avant-garde composer

explanation.surface: Composers arrange music in bars for a singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' and 'singer' suggest music, but the bars are a cage's and the singer is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: A birdcage is a structure of bars housing a songbird such as a canary.

clue.text: Fast runner, but bad player, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the words are spoken aloud, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: a cheater is a dishonest, bad player of a game

explanation.surface: A quick runner turns out to be a dishonest competitor, rumour says.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is the fastest land animal, sprinting at over 100 km/h.

clue.text: Stun all right? Just the opposite, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the letters are spoken aloud, so their spelt-out sound is wanted

parts.note: all right is OK, and just the opposite turns those two letters round, giving the boxing abbreviation for knockout

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a stunned boxer is all right.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters for a knockout, said aloud as letter names, are written out in this slang spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock out a boxer is to stun them, and the spelling of the initials as said is a slang verb for that.

clue.text: Run after one foreign friend or another

indicators.note: after says the run comes after the friend in the answer

parts.note: ami is French for a friend
to go is to run, as a machine goes

explanation.surface: A runner chases a pal from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: AMI is one foreign (French) friend; the answer is another one, the Spanish word.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is the Spanish word for friend, another foreign friend beside the French one.

clue.text: Special food made by workers cooking jolly early

indicators.note: cooking means preparing by mixing, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Kitchen staff prepare a special dish cheerfully early in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'workers' are worker bees, not kitchen staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker bees secrete a rich substance fed to larvae that become queen bees.

clue.text: Plastered house, a work of art

parts.note: plastered and lit are both slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A plastered house turns out to be a work of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' suggests walls coated in plaster, but it means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A litho is short for lithograph, a print made from a flat stone or plate.

clue.text: This thing possibly worn by sleeper, finally

definitions.text: This thing possibly worn by sleeper, finally

indicators.note: possibly signals another arrangement of the letters could be made
finally means at the end, so the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A garment that may be worn in bed at the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges THIS THING with R, the last letter of 'sleeper' given by 'finally'.
explanation.definitionFit: A long loose garment worn in bed is exactly what a sleeper might wear at night.

clue.text: River's watering hole

definitions.meaning: a river in central Europe, flowing through Innsbruck to the Danube
a pub or tavern where people go to drink

explanation.definitionFit: The word names an Alpine river and is also an old word for a pub, a place to drink.

clue.text: American's being taken out for meal in African country

definitions.text: American's being taken out for meal
definitions.meaning: in American usage food ordered to take away is ordered for carrying out
a small West African nation between Ghana and Benin

explanation.surface: A US diner orders takeaway in a West African state.
explanation.definitionFit: The two words split mean takeaway food in American English, and joined they name a country in West Africa.

clue.text: Not well, ie sick

explanation.definitionFit: Poorly can be an adverb meaning badly and an adjective meaning ill.

clue.text: Initiate change in telephony after losing line

indicators.note: change means alter the order, so the remaining letters are rearranged
after losing means once a letter has been taken away

explanation.surface: A newcomer brings in changes to the phone system after a line is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after losing' drops L from TELEPHONY, leaving TEEPHONY, which 'change' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a beginner, a new initiate into a religious order or activity.
